blocker_report.tried: the #K2-454 sec.2.5 capability window in full: (1) sec.20 three questions for the new sub-problem, backfilled; (2) a deterministic start-side substitution (an edge whose BOTH ends lie outside the C35 wall is re-expressed as port <-> port) with a named same-island no-op guard; (3) the rule narrowed to BOTH-outside only after the first dry-run measured that substituting a single outside end cost adds (68 -> 66); (4) sec.16.3 four elements + buildability=no_move + a coverage table; RED->GREEN regression (unit + real-core); selftest 144/144; then the gate dry-run and the conditional N=1.
blocker_report.why_not_yet: C1=2, unchanged. The fix is now PROVEN to be purely a noise/speed fix: the ledger matches the dry-run exactly and the C9 geometric digest is IDENTICAL to R1430 => no geometry changed; the maze stage went 31 min -> ~1 min and 245 former "blocks" are proven same-island no-ops that never needed routing. The two residuals are therefore NOT start-side: I2C2_SCL is a free-space disconnection (its port -> U1.pad22 direction already runs and exhausts with no path at all), and I2C1_SDA is a drawing-side pair (0.6mm F.Cu stub vs 0.2mm B.Cu stub).
blocker_report.gap_layer: TWO layers, now separated: (a) ENGINE MEANS layer - the free-space disconnection of I2C2_SCL needs the collision settlement (rip-up-and-reroute / negotiated congestion, i.e. pass 2), which is now the RELEVANT means rather than a spare one; (b) DRAWING layer - I2C1_SDA is a 0.6mm F.Cu / 0.2mm B.Cu pair on the frozen drawing side, and per sec.16.2 that layer call belongs to the supervisor. The start-side class itself is closed (asset + RED->GREEN), but its binding criterion (C1<2) is unmet, so its capability entry stays open.

plan_recap.q2_what_blocks: For 245 of the old "blocks" nothing at all: they were already the same piece of copper and the tool was being asked to connect a thing to itself (that is now named, and the run got 30x faster). What blocks the last two wires is different in each case: one is a wire whose way is physically taken by other nets (the tool looks, and there is simply no path left), the other is a pair of stubs that sit on different layers and were never joined on the drawing side.

For the second: add the missing join on the drawing side, as a proper sec.16.3 piece with its own conservation and buildability, once the supervisor confirms the layer call.
